result:
The review found 8 distinct bugs. The debugger and the challenger found the same 8 independently, and my own read agrees. Neither specialist could run code, because both had no Bash or Write tool in this session. I haven't run anything either, so each failing input comes from tracing the code by hand.

| Line | Function | Defect |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | `Counter` | `counts = {}` is a class attribute, so all instances share one dict. With `a, b = Counter(), Counter()`, calling `a.add("x")` leaves `b.counts == {"x": 1}`. |
| 11 | `stamp` | The default `datetime.now()` is evaluated once, when the function is defined. Every call without `when` gets the import time, not the time of the call. |
| 17 | `make_multipliers` | The lambdas look up `i` late, so all three use `i == 2`. `[f(5) for f in make_multipliers()]` gives `[10, 10, 10]`, not `[0, 5, 10]`. |
| 21 | `is_valid_id` | `re.match` does not anchor the end, so `"ABC12345"` and `"ABC1234xyz"` return True. `\d` also matches non-ASCII digits. |
| 30 | `find` | `while lo < hi` never checks the last remaining index. `find([5], 5)` and `find([1,2,3], 1)` return -1 although the target is present. |
| 42 | `remove_negatives` | It removes items while iterating, which skips the element after each removal. `[-1, -2, 3]` ends as `[-2, 3]`. |
| 52 | `total_cents` | It sums binary floats and truncates with `int()`. `0.29 * 100` is `28.999999999999996`, so `total_cents(["0.29"])` returns 28, not 29. |
| 60 | `copy_grid` | It is a shallow copy, so the rows are shared. Setting `c[0][0] = 9` on the copy changes the original grid. |

Both specialists judged `clamp`, `chunks_of`, `same_object` and `first_word` correct. I agree. `chunks_of` with `n <= 0` is a missing precondition, not a contradiction of its docstring. The `stamp` shallow copy of nested values is not a defect either, because the docstring doesn't promise a deep copy.
